set.title: Parallel rows
set.stimulus:
Ten persons sit in two parallel rows of five persons each, with equal distance between adjacent persons. Persons in Row 1 face south and persons in Row 2 face north, so each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2. Gopal, Leela, Tarun, Varun and Yash sit in Row 1, and Charu, Eshwar, Jatin, Nitin and Omkar sit in Row 2, not necessarily in the same order. Left and right are taken from each person's own point of view.

1. Only one person sits between Varun and Yash when counted from the right of Varun.
2. Nitin sits to the immediate right of Omkar.
3. Nitin sits third to the left of Eshwar.
4. Gopal sits second to the left of Varun.
5. Charu sits second to the right of Nitin.
6. Varun sits to the immediate right of the one who sits second to the left of Tarun.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits second to the left of Jatin?

steps: Start with clues 1, 4 and 6: together they fix Varun, Yash, Gopal and Tarun.
Clue 3 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Eshwar placed and Nitin placed; Case 2: Eshwar in seat 5 from the west end and Nitin in seat 2 from the west end.
Clue 2 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 2 and 5 then place Omkar and Charu.
Leela takes the only seat left.
Jatin takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — Yash, Tarun, Varun, Leela, Gopal; Row 2 — Omkar, Nitin, Jatin, Charu, Eshwar.
Jatin faces north, so Jatin's right is towards the east end.
Second to the left of Jatin: Nitin → Omkar — answer **Omkar**.
solution.shortcut: Take left/right from the person’s own facing, then count seats along the row.
solution.trap: Eshwar is second to the right — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

questions.prompt: Who are the immediate neighbours of Nitin?

steps: Start with clues 1, 4 and 6: together they fix Varun, Yash, Gopal and Tarun.
Clue 3 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Eshwar placed and Nitin placed; Case 2: Eshwar in seat 5 from the west end and Nitin in seat 2 from the west end.

Clues 2 and 5 then place Omkar and Charu.

Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — Yash, Tarun, Varun, Leela, Gopal; Row 2 — Omkar, Nitin, Jatin, Charu, Eshwar.
On either side of Nitin sit Omkar and Jatin — **Jatin and Omkar**.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Four of the following five pairs are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and so form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group?

steps: Start with clues 1, 4 and 6: together they fix Varun, Yash, Gopal and Tarun.
Clue 3 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Eshwar placed and Nitin placed; Case 2: Eshwar in seat 5 from the west end and Nitin in seat 2 from the west end.
Clue 2 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 2 and 5 then place Omkar and Charu.
Leela takes the only seat left.
Jatin takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — Yash, Tarun, Varun, Leela, Gopal; Row 2 — Omkar, Nitin, Jatin, Charu, Eshwar.
In "Leela, Varun", "Omkar, Nitin", "Charu, Eshwar" and "Jatin, Charu", the second person sits to the immediate right of the first.
In "Varun, Yash", Yash sits second to the right of Varun — so **Varun, Yash** is the odd one.
solution.shortcut: Find the relation in the first two pairs (same direction, same count), then test the rest.
solution.trap: Check direction from the first person’s own facing — a pair that is the same distance but on the other side does not belong.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true according to the given arrangement?
options: Yash sits third to the left of Leela
Nitin is an immediate neighbour of Eshwar
Gopal sits second to the left of Leela
Varun is an immediate neighbour of Omkar
Yash is not an immediate neighbour of Varun

steps: Start with clues 1, 4 and 6: together they fix Varun, Yash, Gopal and Tarun.
Clue 3 gives 2 cases — Case 1: Eshwar placed and Nitin placed; Case 2: Eshwar in seat 5 from the west end and Nitin in seat 2 from the west end.
Clue 2 cannot be met in Case 1, so it is rejected.
Clues 2 and 5 then place Omkar and Charu.
Leela takes the only seat left.
Jatin takes the only seat left.
The chain fits into the row in only one way.
Final arrangement (west to east): Row 1 — Yash, Tarun, Varun, Leela, Gopal; Row 2 — Omkar, Nitin, Jatin, Charu, Eshwar.
(A) Yash sits third to the left of Leela — false.
(B) Nitin is an immediate neighbour of Eshwar — false.
(C) Gopal sits second to the left of Leela — false.
(D) Varun is an immediate neighbour of Omkar — false.
(E) Yash is not an immediate neighbour of Varun — **true**.
solution.shortcut: Test each statement on the final diagram, not on the clue list.
solution.trap: A statement copied from a clue with one word changed (left ↔ right, second ↔ third) looks familiar but is wrong.
